Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion - next steps

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — leadership approved moving forward with a Dedicated deployment for our core inference traffic (sensitive PII workload). Procurement asked me to capture a couple things before we lock schedule:

- Target go-live window: Dec 20–31 preferred (end-of-year ops freeze window is a blocker after Jan).
- Expected sustained throughput: ~55 rps (avg), with 8k token per request average; peak bursts ~220 rps for short windows.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for 2k token slices, but we'll accept fallback for very long prompts.
- Model set: mix of Llama2-70B-Chat (quantized) and a custom fine-tuned 13B for retrieval-augmented answers.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can validate sizing within our timeline and provide an initial cutover plan? Procurement copied.

Thanks,
Daniel
Platform Lead, Aegis Financial

Daniel —

This is doable but tight; thanks for the traffic numbers. To validate sizing and produce a cutover timeline we need the following within 48 hours:

1) token distribution percentiles (p50/p90/p99) and % of requests that need full context vs. short context.
2) expected concurrent sessions (chat-like flows) vs. single-shot generation.
3) retention/PKI constraints (do you need on-prem HSM for keys?).
4) whether you require guaranteed reserved GPU pool vs. hybrid reserved + burst.

Connor and Laura will run an early-cost/throughput sketch and a staging runbook once we have the token percentiles. If you can share the CSV snapshot, we’ll iterate quickly and attach a sizing workbook.

Proposed immediate milestone:
- 11/04: Redwood returns a first-pass GPU fleet sketch + MAP (mutual action plan)
- 11/09: Aegis provides token percentiles + security questionnaire answers
- 11/13–11/17: Validation runs in staging (customer-supplied sample traffic)
- 11/20–11/22: Canary cutover (traffic split 10/90 -> 50/50 -> 100%)
- 12/20–12/31: Target final cutover (per your preference)

I’ll attach the initial MAP and a blank sizing workbook.

—Vanessa
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -07:00

Vanessa —

Initial sizing sketch attached. High-level notes (quick, back-of-envelope):

- Model mix assumption: 70% Llama2-70B quantized (8-bit), 30% custom-13B (4-bit).
- Average tokens/request: 8k as stated; average generation per request ~1.2k tokens.
- Concurrency targets: given 55 sustained rps -> assume 55 concurrent short-lived requests, but chat sessions inflate KV cache requirements; plan for 600 concurrent chat sessions at peak to be safe.

Preliminary recommendation:
- Baseline pool: 24 x A100-80GB (or equivalent H100-80GB) for steady-state (covers 55 rps sustain with batching + prefix cache).
- Burst pool: additional 12 x A100 reserved for sudden spikes (220 rps peaks) with auto-burst policy and graceful fallback to smaller quantized variants.
- Staging: 6 x A100 for smoke + canary runs.

Notes on timeline risk: procurement and HSM onboarding can add 3–5 business days. If Aegis needs private key footprint in their VPC, factor that into the 11/13 validation window.

Connor O'Brien
Infra Engineering (Serving Runtime), Redwood Inference
